raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.5.0"

package:
  name: vmprof
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/vmprof/vmprof-python/archive/${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 0b92e51c579b3439747a2d754c721a884624381a72fb59e238c6357a8028551d

build:
  number: 1
  script:
    - if: not (ppc64le or aarch64)
      then: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv
      else: LDFLAGS+=" -pthread" ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv
  python:
    entry_points:
      - vmprofshow = vmprof.show:main

requirements:
  build:
    - if: build_platform != target_platform
      then:
        - python
        - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
  host:
    - python
    - pip
    - meson-python >=0.17
    - if: linux
      then: libunwind
  run:
    - python
    - requests
    - colorama
    - six
    - if: linux
      then: libunwind

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - vmprof
        - jitlog
        - vmshare
      pip_check: false
  - files:
      source:
        - vmprof
        - src
    requirements:
      run:
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - zlib
        - pytest
        - cffi
        - hypothesis
        - setuptools >=77
    script:
      - vmprofshow --help
      - if: not (ppc64le or aarch64 or win)
        then:
          # The cffi test extensions are built with "-Werror -O0". glibc emits a
          # (fatal under -Werror) warning for _FORTIFY_SOURCE without -O, so
          # undefine it after conda-forge's CFLAGS have defined it. distutils
          # appends CPPFLAGS after CFLAGS, so it must be undefined there too.
          - export CFLAGS="${CFLAGS} -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE"
          - export CPPFLAGS="${CPPFLAGS} -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE"
          # test_resolve_addr stores the resolved source path in a 128-byte
          # buffer. rattler-build's test-files directory is too deep for that,
          # so run the tests from a short temporary path.
          - tmpdir=$(mktemp -d) && cp -r vmprof src "$tmpdir" && cd "$tmpdir"
          - CC=$CC_FOR_BUILD py.test vmprof/ -vrs
      - if: win
        then: py.test vmprof/ -vrs

about:
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE
  summary: vmprof - a statistical program profiler
  description: |
    vmprof is a platform to understand and resolve performance bottlenecks in your code.
    It includes a lightweight profiler for CPython 2.7, CPython 3 and PyPy and
    an assembler log visualizer for PyPy.
  homepage: https://github.com/vmprof/vmprof-python
  repository: https://github.com/vmprof/vmprof-python
  documentation: https://vmprof.readthedocs.io

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - synapticarbors
    - matthiasdiener
    - mattip
